# Encounter seed-row legality cross-check — env_0073 tasks 0 and 1

Criterion: published docs in docs/encounter/*.json (title+content). Context: claims/plan/estimate/assistance rows in the same dumps. Frozen: T0 2025-10-21, T1 2025-11-18.

Arithmetic verified by script for every account: gross_charges_total = sum of charge lines; patient_balance = liabilities − adjustments − payments; final_bill_date = service end + class bill-hold days (Recurring: last day of month + 5); every insured liability equals the claim's PR remit (same date, same claim id); every CT liability equals the PR-27 denial; every plan-installment payment equals a plan_installment_paid row (ref, date, amount); every first_statement_date equals the seq-1 summary row.

## 2. MISS list

**None.** No seeded account, transaction or inquiry row of either task contradicts a published encounter rule, and none is a row the published rules could not have produced. Every row in the table is OK.

## 3. Owed adjustments not yet posted at the frozen time (not counted as MISS)

The docs say these are owed. But none of them is automatic at a stated date: each is posted with an agent-side tool ("the representative unlocks ... then calls it"). The docs also expect the unposted state. The owed courtesy exists for statements "issued while its coverage-terminated postings carried no uninsured discount", and courtesy §3 expects a self-pay observation account whose observation-rate discount does not stand yet. So these are open items in a world the docs allow. They are probably task targets. All of them lower an encounter balance, and the assistance program reads those balances.

- **O1. T0 E2 (8bdb031d, Clinic, CT 420.00 on 2025-03-27, txn 53b51ab0).** No UNINSURED_DISCOUNT row. coverage_terminated_uninsured_discount_posting: "One uninsured discount adjustment is owed on them, sourced to the account's most recent coverage-terminated posting". Starting percent is the Clinic uninsured 40 (coverage_loss_discount_calculation), plus any factors. This lowers the 420.00 balance enrolled in plan 3d0a5ecb. **Could change an assistance figure:** the open T0 hardship application (case 43c615c2, submitted) will read the patient's encounter balances, and E2 is part of them.
- **O2. T0 E2 owed service-recovery courtesy.** The seq-1 summary statement (a3189277, 2025-04-01) went out while the CT posting carried no discount. owed_service_recovery_courtesy_posting §1: "one service-recovery courtesy adjustment is owed for that failure whether or not the patient reports it". §3 says it is fixed only after the CT discount stands. See doc observation X1: the balance is under an active plan. Balance effect only; Clinic maximum 25.00.
- **O3. T0 E3 (c88c4cb6, Observation, self-pay, FB 2025-07-01).** It has observation-hour line fb9b0219 (0762, 22 h, 4840.00), but there is no observation-rate UNINSURED_DISCOUNT. The account is not package-priced. observation_rate_discount_posting: "Riverbend's self-pay observation rate is granted as one uninsured discount adjustment, sourced to the account's most recent observation-hour charge line"; its table: "observation-hour charge lines, final bill dropped, no package price | that one, plus one observation-rate discount". On the published text the figure would be: days 1 (22 h is not above 24 × 1), day rate 1250 + 250 (Appleton with a 0450 line) = 1500, LOS factor none (<24 h), carve-out none (no 0350/0480 line), giving (4840 − 1500) × 0.5 = **1670.00**. The 5% floor is 242.00. This would lower the 3950.00 enrolled balance. **Could change an assistance figure** (same open application). Note: the final-bill uninsured discount is automatic ("the uninsured discount follows"), but no doc fixes when the observation-rate discount must post. So this is not a MISS.
- **O4. T1 E2 (15c52208, Clinic, ELECTIVE, CT 1180.00 on 2025-06-13, txn 61f96743).** No CT uninsured discount. Same rule as O1. The starting percent is the elective 20 (coverage_loss_discount_calculation). It lowers the 1180.00 enrolled in plan 7496ef5b. It could change an assistance figure if the assistance product reads this balance. No assist_encounter_applied row exists for E2 today.
- **O5. T1 E2 owed courtesy.** The seq-1 summary a1627255 (2025-06-17) went out with no CT discount. Same rule as O2. Clinic maximum 25.00. See X1.
- **O6. T1 E6 (bd2c77fb, Clinic, CT 830.00 on 2025-11-17, txn 8888db53).** The CT discount is owed. The posting is one day old and no statement has been issued, so no courtesy is owed yet.

No other required adjustment is missing:
- No NON_COVERED_SERVICE liability exists in either task, so no non-covered discount is owed.
- No payment is a full payoff, so no prompt-pay discount is owed.
- No balance is in (0, 4.99], so no small-balance write-off is owed.
- No late charge: every charge posted on or before its final bill date.
- No credit balance needs a refund. The only one, T0 E8's 40.00 POS payment from 09-09 to 09-24, was absorbed by the copay within 30 days.

## 4. Doubtful (not a miss)

- **D1. Summary statements stop after plan enrollment.** This affects T0 E0 (after the final notice), E1, E2, E3, E4, E5 and T1 E0, E2, E3. statement_cycle_and_collection_actions says a patient-due account with balance ≥ 5.00 "receives a summary statement every statement cycle", with no plan exception in the encounter docs. However, every enrollment happened before the second cycle date: T0 E1 03-12 < 03-26; E2 04-10 < 05-01; E3 07-08 < 08-03; E4 05-20 < 06-07; E5 07-08 < 08-01; T1 E0 03-03 < 03-11; E2 07-01 < 07-17; E3 07-20 < 08-11. The plan docs (cross-product) say that on default or cancellation the enrolled accounts "resume the standard statement cycle from where it stopped" / "return to the standard statement cycle". So enrolled balances are off the cycle by design. T0 E0 is a separate case. After its final notice (2025-01-18) no statement issued before enrollment (03-12), although a cycle date (02-17) fell between them. The docs only say "the next statement is a final notice" and say nothing about statements after the final notice. Placement day 150 = 2025-03-19, after enrollment, so no placement was owed.
- **D2. A patient-due account goes on hold before any first statement.** T1 E1: FB 09-26, GFE hold 09-29, FS empty. T1 E4: liabilities 11-10, itemization hold 11-13, FS empty. The seed's own lag is FB+3 for self-pay and liability+4/5 for insured. The docs fix no first-statement lag, and "An account on billing hold receives no statement beyond the current cycle". Both holds meet billing_hold_policy: the account was patient-due, the reason has a record condition (an in_dispute estimate linked to the account) or a request (an itemized request inquiry the same day), and holds used = 1 ≤ 2.
- **D3. T0 E7 ITEMIZATION_REVIEW hold still live at 10-21 after the itemized statement issued 10-09.** billing_hold_policy: "released when its reason is resolved or its length lapses". The inquiry is still IN_REVIEW, so the review is not shown resolved. The 30-day length runs to 11-05.

Across worlds, T1 uses 4500030 → 99283. T0 E1 line 1 is revenue code 0120 (room & board) carrying CPT 99223 × 5 units. No published rule governs CDM↔CPT mapping. The duplicate-line test is within one account only, so nothing changes.
- **D5. T1 E6 coverage-terminated timing.** Quartz PR-27 says coverage terminated before 10-28, yet Quartz adjudicated E4 (svc 10-20) with cost-sharing. This is possible with a termination between 10-21 and 10-27, and the new payer (Security Health) is on E5 by 11-09. This is a claim-product matter, not an encounter rule.
